title: Physics-Guided Machine Learning for Scientific Discovery: An Application in Simulating Lake Temperature Profiles
testbed_rationale: The 1D lake thermal dynamics problem provides a well-defined benchmark for physics-guided machine learning, loss-function-based energy conservation constraints, and synthetic-data pre-training across sparse observational regimes.
pain_points: Extreme sparsity of observational field data (most lakes have <1% of required observations)
Black-box ML predictions violate basic thermodynamic conservation laws (energy/mass)
Process models (GLM) carry structural biases in vertical stratification dynamics at intermediate and bottom depths
Model generalization to unseen climate regimes, novel lake geometries, and distinct water clarity conditions
extraction_notes: The paper builds on and refines the experiments originally reported in Jia et al. [2019] and Read et al. [2019]. Observational and driver data are pointed to the USGS / NTL-LTER repositories cited via Read et al. [2019].
